title: Fixed neuron degrees permit removal of an adjusted response wiring slope in one MICrONS mouse
abstract: We tested whether fixed neuron counts protect a response wiring slope from selective label changes. The MICrONS v1 panel had 295,371 candidate directions and 8,128 connections from one mouse. We fixed every source and target degree and each source output count by anatomical opportunity group. A binary example removed the adjusted measured movie correlation slope with 208 additions and the same number of deletions. A checked continuous bound required at least 208 relocations. A rank score required between 259 and 259. These are sensitivity bounds, not measured error rates. One mouse, selected candidates, coarse anatomy controls and fixed response estimates limit transfer. Code, compact input, witnesses, numerical certificates and a figure permit reproduction.

display.caption: Lower bounds and binary examples for fixed-margin label changes in one mouse. One relocation adds and deletes one direction. This is a sensitivity test, not an error estimate.

citations.reason: Extends the selective missing-edge question to equal additions and deletions with both degrees fixed. No code or numerical input reused.
